description:
# Remove repeated container slugs from archive destinations

## Problem

The development-root cutover removed paths shaped like dev/archive/<container>/dev/..., but retained a second owner copy when a source already lives under an area/container directory. The tracked tree currently contains 54 paths shaped like dev/archive/<container>/<area>/<container>/..., including active and presentations artifacts for 8e071e18-dev-artifact-layout and active artifacts for a2546471-json-error-contract. This repeats ownership rather than adding hierarchy and creates the same long-path failure mode as the rejected development-root duplication.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Archive destination derivation strips both the configured development root and a matching area/container owner prefix, producing dev/archive/<container>/<area>/<artifact-relative-path> without a repeated container slug.
- [hard] Preview and execution use the same canonical destination derivation, preserve collision safety, and cover active plus non-active managed areas with positive and negative regressions.
- [hard] All 54 current repeated-owner archive paths and their live repository references are migrated to the canonical layout without rewriting immutable event history or history-only prose.
- [hard] A repository regression check rejects dev/archive/<container>/<area>/<container>/... and analogous repeated owner nesting while allowing legitimate vendored names such as reveal.js/reveal.js.
- [hard] Current adopter and contributor documentation states archive paths relative to development_root and container ownership exactly once; projections and link validation remain clean.

## Non-goals

- Renaming third-party vendored directories whose repeated name is part of the upstream package layout.
- Rewriting immutable event records or historical narrative that only describes the former path.
title: Remove repeated container slugs from archive destinations
